title: Residual Variance Price of the Gram-Schmidt Walk Design at Boundary Robustness Calibration
banked_reason: The promised fixed-phi, rate-tight actual-walk residual frontier is still explicitly open; delivered local diagnostics and reductions are incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The promised fixed-phi, rate-tight actual-walk residual frontier is still explicitly open: the proved changing-robustness boundary upper bound and fixed-n local diagnostic neither give its evaluable scale, matching bounded witnesses, zero-regime classification, nor limits, so the current artifact has no theorem-level novelty or usable headline deliverable on the stated problem.

Open-ended Question sharp-residual-frontier contains the entire requested fixed-robustness asymptotic result: no comparison scale, limiting price, dimension dependence, or asymptotically attaining sequence is delivered. The changing-robustness boundary bound is inherited from [Cytrynbaum Theorem 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.18057v1#S5), and its explicit constant follows directly from the existing covariance envelope. The new quartic inflation calculation applies only when 1-phi is at most 1/[4(n-1)], with an exponentially growing remainder constant, so it supplies no fixed-phi asymptotic lower bound. The ATE inequality retains an unevaluated supremum, while residual-coefficient optimality transfers that defining supremum into causal laws without evaluating its magnitude. The framing discloses these limitations and contains no stale claim of a proved sharp frontier, but the delivered content remains local diagnostics and reductions rather than the contracted variance characterization. The projected score is constrained by the absence of a quantitative fixed-parameter guarantee that could inform the stated software and experimental-design consumers; editorial improvement cannot supply that result.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery retained the actual retained-pivot assignment and the full bounded population residual class, deriving finite-n diagnostics and a causal variance transfer. Maximality review added the credited changing-robustness boundary, and four exact source attestations passed the math referee. The fixed-robustness rate, matching witnesses, zero regimes, and limits remain open; novelty is incremental below field, confirmed independently. No F stage or Lean proof was attempted.
tldr: At the published boundary calibration \(\phi^{\mathrm b}_{n,d}=1-\min\{1/2,(d^2\log n/n)^{1/2}\}\), Cytrynbaum Theorem 5.3 implies \(0\le q_n-1\le C(d^2\log n/n)^{1/2}\) for the entire bounded residual class, and hence \(q_n\to1\) in the stated dimension regime. The inherited covariance envelope permits the explicit constant \(C=2\). At a fixed public \(\phi<1\), the rate above one, exact-zero cases beyond the proved two-unit case, limiting value, and bounded attaining sequences remain open. The same actual retained-pivot law and original population residual class are used throughout. Once evaluated, \(q_n\) is the optimal residual-only ATE variance coefficient; the causal variance transfer and structured remainder are already proved.
gap: Cytrynbaum gives a coefficient-one bivariate guarantee with robustness approaching one and a faster fixed-robustness result under well specification. Chatterjee, Dey, and Goswami identify finite-feature empirical residual variance. Neither verified statement determines \(q_n(\phi,d)\) for the full near-critical kernel and population residual class.
fill: Open-ended Question 1 requires an evaluable scale with matching bounds, bounded deterministic witnesses, and a complete limit classification. Theorem 2 translates that answer into ATE precision. Theorem 3 certifies optimality of the residual coefficient with zero structured remainder.
